No — I'd rate this higher than Quick, and recommend against self-approval/skip-review here, even though it's a one-line diff.

**Why it's not actually "tiny":**
- `ENFORCE_MFA_FOR_ADMINS` is a global flag in a *shared* config used across all backend services. Flipping it doesn't just unblock one admin — it removes MFA enforcement for *every* admin, everywhere, for however long it's live.
- It crosses an authentication/security trust boundary, which is exactly the kind of change that benefits from a second set of eyes, even a fast one.
- "Revert in an hour" relies on a human remembering under time pressure — a very plausible way for a security control to silently stay disabled (person gets pulled away, deploy hiccups, PR sits unmerged, etc.), with no one else aware it happened.

**What I'd do instead:**
1. **Fix the actual problem, not the blast-radius-wide proxy for it.** Most auth setups let you reset/bypass MFA for a *single* user account (identity provider admin console, backup codes, support tool) instead of toggling a global enforcement flag. That's the same speed with none of the exposure to other admins.
2. If the global flag truly is the only lever available, still get a quick second approval (even an async Slack thumbs-up from another engineer) rather than self-approving — the point isn't process for its own sake, it's having someone other than the person under pressure double-check the revert actually happens.
3. Don't rely on memory for the revert: open the "flip back to True" PR immediately alongside the flip-to-false one, or set a hard alert/monitor so an unrevert is caught automatically, not an hour later when someone remembers.

Want help checking whether your identity provider supports a per-user MFA reset, so you can avoid touching the global flag entirely?
